candidates.fit: WINNER (family A/B front end): 2.2-36V single supply fits the 3.3V rail; ~12-13kHz BW at G150-165 clears the 7kHz target (better still, 20kHz, run at G~100 for the Family B split); CMRR 120dB min G>=100; REF needs a low-Z buffer (classic topology, Fig.59) - use the Family B second stage for that instead of a dedicated buffer.

Family B/C second stage: 1.8-5.5V RRIO zero-drift dual, closes AD8226's gain to ~165 and injects the ~0.1V pedestal at its own summing node (AD8226 REF then just grounds - no buffer IC needed). Its own offset/drift/noise are divided by total system gain (~165) once referred to input - negligible either way.

Family A runner-up: only part found with a HIGH-Z REF pin (ICF architecture - datasheet states resistance at REF has no effect on CMRR), saves the buffer a classic in-amp needs. BUT BW at G150-165 is ~6.1-6.7kHz with the BW pin strapped to +VS - zero to negative margin against the 7kHz/1% target, and a wrong strap is a real assembly risk.

DISQUALIFIED for this board: needs 4.5-36V single supply, this rail is 3.13-3.47V. Otherwise excellent - 160-180kHz BW at G150-165 (huge margin), 7nV/rtHz noise, 130dB CMRR - kept in the list because it is the cleanest proof that bandwidth-capable classic in-amps and 3.3V-compatible in-amps are largely disjoint sets.

DISQUALIFIED for this board: 2.2-36V supply is fine, but BW is only ~1.9-2.1kHz at G150-165 (datasheet tabulates 3kHz@G100, 0.4kHz@G1000) - well under the 7kHz target. Best-in-class output swing (7-25mV from each rail at 100k) if a lower-gain role ever fits.

DISQUALIFIED for this board: 2.7-36V supply is fine, but BW is only 2.5kHz at G=100 already (datasheet-tabulated) - the exact 'micropower trades away bandwidth' case requirements.md 9a warns against. REF impedance is a third, gain-compensable category (neither free divider nor strict low-Z).
